Use these four US size brackets and multiplier tables to benchmark any commercial janitorial bid.
quickAnswer: The average office cleaning cost per square foot in the US ranges from $0.05 to $0.20 per sq ft per visit, spanning four size tiers: $0.12–$0.20/sq ft under 2,500 sq ft, $0.09–$0.15/sq ft for 2,500–9,999 sq ft, $0.07–$0.12/sq ft for 10,000–24,999 sq ft, and $0.05–$0.10/sq ft at 25,000+ sq ft. Adding $15 to $30 per restroom, flooring multipliers, and $90–$135 visit minimums shifts the real effective rate.

blocks.text: Asking a janitorial contractor for a flat rate per square foot without defining restroom count, floor finishes, or weekly visit frequency is the fastest way to receive an unusable quote. While US facility buyers rely on per-square-foot averages to build initial operating budgets, legitimate proposals only use square footage as **one input** inside a multi-variable labor formula.

Across the [national office cleaning cost guides](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/) benchmark dataset, base rates compress by more than 50% as footprints scale from 1,000 sq ft to 50,000+ sq ft because travel time, security sign-in, and equipment staging dilute across larger areas. Understanding where your suite sits—and which surcharges sit outside the base rate—prevents surprise change orders after move-in.
2026 US Office Cleaning Rates Across All Four Size Brackets

Commercial cleaning companies group offices into four standardized square-footage brackets. Suites under 2,500 sq ft absorb full technician mobilization overhead across minimal floor area and frequently collide with the **$90 to $135 minimum per-visit charge**. Conversely, facilities above 25,000 sq ft achieve steady-state production near ISSA's **3,500 sq ft per labor hour** average, dropping base unit rates to **$0.05 to $0.10 per sq ft**.

blocks.title: Why Effective Rate Differs From Quoted Base Rate
blocks.text: Notice that a 1,000 sq ft office in a $0.12–$0.20/sq ft bracket actually pays $0.145–$0.246/sq ft effective once one restroom ($15–$30/visit) and weekly frequency adjustment (1.08x) are added. Meanwhile, a 50,000 sq ft 5x/week floor benefits from a 0.90x daily discount, pulling effective total cost to $0.049–$0.097/sq ft.
Why Two Offices With Identical Square Footage Receive Different Quotes

If two competing bids for your suite differ by 25% per square foot, the gap almost always comes from four built-in multipliers or excluded add-ons rather than contractor profit alone. Hard floors that demand damp mopping and machine buffing require slower passes than wide-aisle carpet vacuuming, and infrequent schedules collect heavier soil between visits.

blocks.text: Rentable vs. Cleanable Square Footage: Avoiding the BOMA Load-Factor Trap

Commercial real estate leases routinely state **rentable square footage (RSF)**—which adds an 12% to 22% BOMA building load factor for shared ground-floor lobbies, elevator banks, stairwells, and mechanical shafts that your landlord's building engineer already cleans. Providing your RSF number to janitorial bidders inflates your cleaning invoice for hallways your crew never touches.

blocks.title: Measure Net Cleanable Footage Before Requesting Quotes
blocks.text: On a 12,000 RSF lease with an 18% load factor, usable cleanable area inside your suite may be only 9,840 sq ft—dropping you from a 10,000+ sq ft estimate into a cleaner footprint minus 2,160 non-serviced square feet. Subtract server closets, dead storage rooms, and landlord-maintained corridors before inviting walkthroughs.
Labor-Hour Math Behind Every Legitimate Per-Square-Foot Bid

Every square-foot rate ultimately converts back to **burdened labor hours**. Under ISSA commercial production benchmarks (**2,800 to 4,000 sq ft per hour**, averaging 3,500 sq ft/hr, plus **0.15 to 0.25 hours per restroom**), a 5,000 sq ft suite with two restrooms requires **1.55 to 2.29 hours per visit**. At standard US contractor billing of **$35 to $65 per hour** (see our [commercial janitorial hourly rates guide](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/commercial-janitorial-hourly-rates-guide/)), any bid dramatically under $0.08/sq ft for a 5,000 sq ft space is mathematically incapable of paying legal W-2 payroll taxes and supervision.

Crew productivity at `$0.05 to $0.15/sq ft` depends heavily on ergonomic, commercial-grade detailing tools that cut rework and OSHA slip-and-fall liability. Across desks and restroom counters, **Rubbermaid Commercial HYGEN Microfiber Damp/Wet Cloths** (12-pack of 16x16 split-microfiber cloths, bleach safe, rated for 500 commercial launderings, color-coded to prevent restroom-to-kitchenette cross-contamination) keep chemical dwell even without streaking. For wet-mopping corridors safely, crews deploy a **Rubbermaid Commercial 36-Inch Yellow Caution Wet Floor Cone** (4-sided bilingual print, stackable, ANSI/OSHA compliant) alongside the **O-Cedar Commercial MaxiClean Angle Broom & Lobby Pan** (12-in flagged poly bristles on a 48-in handle shaped for crisp baseboard edges).
How to Normalize Competing Per-Square-Foot Proposals

Use our [Office Cleaning Cost Calculator](/office-cleaning-cost-calculator/) to establish your target range, then standardize vendor bids in the [Quote Comparator](/compare-cleaning-quotes/) using these five checks.

items.name: Convert All Proposals to Effective Cost per Cleanable Sq Ft
items.text: Divide the quoted per-visit total (including restrooms and breakrooms) by net cleanable square feet rather than comparing stripped base rates.

items.name: Check Whether 4.333 Weeks/Month Was Applied
items.text: Verify that monthly retainers cover 13.00 visits/month (3x/week) or 21.65 visits/month (5x/week) rather than a 4-week 12- or 20-visit cap.

items.name: Audit Floor-Care and Consumables Line Items
items.text: Confirm whether VCT buffing, carpet extraction ($0.03–$0.06/sq ft/mo), and paper supplies ($0.012–$0.025/sq ft/visit) are included or excluded.

items.name: Verify Implied Labor Hours Against ISSA Production Speeds
items.text: Ensure quoted hours stay within 2,800 to 4,000 sq ft/hr plus restroom minutes; check smaller suites against our minimum charge per visit guide.

items.name: Confirm W-2 Insurance, Bond, and HazCom Paperwork
items.text: Require $1M/$2M General Liability COI, Workers' Compensation, fidelity bonding, and OSHA SDS binders before signing.

faqs.q: What is a fair price per square foot for a 5,000 sq ft office?
faqs.a: A 5,000 sq ft office falls into the 2,500–9,999 sq ft bracket ($0.09 to $0.15/sq ft base). With two restrooms ($15–$30 each) on a 3x/week carpeted schedule (0.95x frequency multiplier), total per-visit pricing averages $458 to $773 ($0.092 to $0.155/sq ft effective), or $5,948 to $10,043 per month.

faqs.q: Why do offices under 1,000 sq ft pay more than $0.20 per square foot effectively?
faqs.a: Small suites hit commercial trip minimums ($90 to $135 per visit in average US markets) plus fixed restroom surcharges ($15 to $30 each). Even if floor math calculates to $65, contractors bill the minimum visit fee to cover drive time and a two-hour labor floor.

faqs.q: Are Green Seal chemicals and HEPA vacuums included in standard per-sq-ft rates?
faqs.a: Many mid-to-large US contractors now standardize on Green Seal GS-37 or EPA Safer Choice dilution chemicals and HEPA-filtered vacuums with minimal (0%–4%) price impact, but you must explicitly require them in your RFP scope and verify OSHA HazCom Safety Data Sheets.

faqs.q: What tasks are excluded from standard per-square-foot cleaning prices?
faqs.a: Standard recurring rates exclude hot-water carpet extraction, VCT stripping and waxing, exterior window washing, high-reach dusting above 8–10 feet, inside-refrigerator cleanouts, paper/soap consumables, and OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens biohazard cleanup unless priced as separate line items.

faqs.q: How does 4.333 weeks per month math change annual per-square-foot spend?
faqs.a: Multiplying weekly visits by 4.333 weeks/month (4.33 in rounded pricing tools) gives 13.00 visits/month for 3x/week and 21.65 visits/month for 5x/week. Bids assuming 4.0 weeks/month understate annual cost by 8.3% and frequently trigger fifth-week extra billing.
